title: Troubleshoot Video, Projector, and Display Issues

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Display problems can originate from input selection, cables, projector hardware, display panels, resolution or other settings, and audio configuration. Recognize the symptom and identify the most appropriate area to troubleshoot.
bullets: Incorrect input source and physical cabling
Burnt-out projector bulb
Fuzzy image, burn-in, and dead pixels
Flashing screen and incorrect colors
Audio issues
Dim image and intermittent projector shutdown
Sizing and distorted images
sections.callout: SOURCE → CABLE → DISPLAY → SETTINGS → PROJECTOR → AUDIO

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When a screen looks wrong, shows nothing, loses its image, or a projector behaves incorrectly, identify whether the problem is the input, cable, panel, configuration, or projector hardware.
bullets: Wrong source selected → incorrect input source
Image changes when cable moves → physical cabling
Projector produces no light → burnt-out bulb
Blurry image → fuzzy image
Retained image → burn-in
One fixed bad point → dead pixel
Repeated flicker → flashing screen
Wrong colors → cable, settings, or display
Video without sound → audio path
Very dark image → brightness, backlight, or lamp
Hot projector shuts down → thermal issue
Too large or small → sizing
Stretched or warped → distortion

sections.title: Common Video, Projector, and Display Symptoms
paragraphs: Classify display symptoms before replacing equipment. The same visible result can come from the source, connection, settings, display panel, or projector hardware.
sections.callout: NO SIGNAL → QUALITY → PANEL DEFECT → AUDIO → PROJECTOR → GEOMETRY

sections.title: Start With the Signal Path
bullets: Confirm the source device is producing video.
Verify the correct output is being used.
Select the matching input on the display.
Secure both ends of the cable.
Test the cable or adapter when appropriate.
Verify resolution and display settings.
Test the display or projector itself.
sections.callout: SOURCE → CONNECTION → DISPLAY → CONFIGURATION

sections.title: Incorrect Input Source
paragraphs: Displays and projectors can offer HDMI, DisplayPort, VGA, USB-C, and other inputs. A computer connected to HDMI 2 will not appear when the display is set to HDMI 1.
sections.callout: Laptop is connected but projector says No Signal → verify the input source.

Input matches but signal is missing or intermittent
Inspect and test the physical path

sections.callout: PORT MATCH FIRST.

sections.title: Physical Cabling Issues
paragraphs: A damaged, loose, incorrect, or poorly seated cable can cause no image, intermittent video, flickering, incorrect colors, audio trouble, or reduced quality. Inspect both ends, connectors, adapters, the cable body, and the selected port type.
sections.callout: Display problem → always check the physical path.

sections.title: Intermittent Cable Problems
paragraphs: When moving a video cable causes the image to appear or disappear, the cable or connector is a strong suspect.
sections.callout: MOVEMENT CHANGES THE SYMPTOM → CABLE/CONNECTOR.

sections.title: Burnt-Out Bulb
paragraphs: Many projectors use a lamp that eventually reaches the end of its service life. A failed or failing bulb can produce no projected light, a very dim image before failure, or a lamp warning indicator. Follow manufacturer replacement procedures because lamps can become extremely hot.
sections.callout: Projector powers on but the lamp does not illuminate → burnt-out bulb.

sections.title: Fuzzy Image
paragraphs: A blurry image can result from incorrect focus, resolution, scaling, poor cable quality, projector distance, or positioning. For monitors, verify native resolution and scaling; for projectors, also check focus and distance.
sections.callout: Fuzzy = image exists but lacks clarity.

sections.title: Native Resolution
paragraphs: Flat-panel displays are usually clearest at their intended native resolution. An incorrect resolution can cause blur, scaling artifacts, and sizing problems.
sections.callout: Wrong resolution → image may not look sharp.

sections.title: Display Burn-In
paragraphs: Burn-in occurs when a persistent image becomes permanently retained or visibly imprinted on a display. Static interface elements may remain visible even after the content changes.
sections.callout: OLD IMAGE WILL NOT LEAVE → BURN-IN.

sections.title: Burn-In vs. Temporary Image Retention
paragraphs: Objective 5.3 requires recognition of display burn-in. The key clue is a persistent ghost of previously displayed content rather than a temporary artifact that fades.
sections.callout: Persistent old pattern → burn-in.

sections.title: Dead Pixels
paragraphs: A dead pixel does not operate correctly and can appear as a tiny fixed point that remains in the same location regardless of the displayed image.
sections.callout: Dead pixel = one tiny permanent display defect.

sections.title: Flashing Screen
paragraphs: A flashing or flickering screen can involve a loose or damaged cable, display hardware, refresh settings, graphics hardware or software, or power. Begin with secure connections and correct settings, then test known-good components when appropriate.
sections.callout: Flicker = unstable image path or display behavior.

sections.title: Flashing Screen vs. Intermittent Blank Screen
Incorrect Color Display
paragraphs: Wrong tones, missing colors, an unusual tint, or washed output can result from loose or damaged cabling, bent connector pins, display settings, color configuration, or display hardware.
sections.callout: Strange VGA color tint → inspect the cable and connector pins.

sections.title: Color Settings
paragraphs: If the physical signal path is good, inspect color temperature, profiles, brightness, contrast, and operating-system display configuration.
sections.callout: HARDWARE GOOD → CHECK SETTINGS.

sections.title: Audio Issues
paragraphs: HDMI and some DisplayPort configurations carry video and audio. If the picture works but sound does not, check the selected audio output, interface capability, display speakers, volume and mute controls, and OS audio settings.
sections.callout: Working video does not guarantee correct audio routing.

sections.title: Audio Output Device
paragraphs: A computer can send sound to internal speakers, headphones, an HDMI display, a DisplayPort monitor, or a dock. Selecting the wrong destination can leave display speakers silent even while video works.
sections.callout: HDMI video works but sound goes elsewhere → select the correct audio output.

sections.title: Dim Image
paragraphs: A dim image remains visible but is not bright enough. Causes include brightness settings, a backlight problem, a projector lamp nearing failure, power-saving settings, or display hardware.
sections.callout: IMAGE EXISTS + TOO DARK → BRIGHTNESS/BACKLIGHT/LAMP.

table.caption: Use the device in the scenario
rows: Lamp age, brightness mode, room conditions, hardware

sections.title: Intermittent Projector Shutdown
paragraphs: A projector may shut down to protect itself from excessive heat caused by blocked vents, dust, a failed fan, overheating, or poor airflow.
sections.callout: PROJECTOR RUNS, GETS HOT, THEN SHUTS DOWN → THERMAL.

sections.title: Projector Thermal Protection
paragraphs: Projectors generate substantial heat. Keep vents clear, maintain filters when applicable, verify fans operate, and provide adequate ventilation.
sections.callout: A hot projector protects itself by shutting down.

sections.title: Sizing Issues
paragraphs: A sizing problem makes the image too large, too small, cut off, or unable to fill the expected area. Investigate resolution, scaling, aspect ratio, projector zoom, and display settings.
sections.callout: Correct shape, wrong overall size → configuration or geometry.

sections.title: Resolution and Scaling
paragraphs: Inappropriate operating-system resolution or scaling can make text and windows appear too large or too small.
sections.callout: SIZE PROBLEM → RESOLUTION/SCALING.

sections.title: Distorted Image
paragraphs: A distorted image has the wrong shape or proportions, such as stretched, squashed, warped, or trapezoid output. Causes include aspect-ratio settings, resolution mismatch, projector alignment, and keystone settings.
sections.callout: Distortion = shape is wrong.

sections.title: Projector Keystone Distortion
paragraphs: A projector that is not perpendicular to the screen can produce a trapezoid-shaped image. Correct projector position first and use keystone correction when appropriate.
sections.callout: Projected image wider at one end → position or keystone correction.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Display set to a different port → incorrect input source
Signal changes when cable moves → physical cabling
Projector lamp fails to illuminate → burnt-out bulb
Blurry image → fuzzy image
Old image remains visible → burn-in
One permanent bad point → dead pixel
Rapid display flicker → flashing screen
Strange tint or missing color → incorrect color display
HDMI picture without sound → audio issue or output selection
Visible but dark picture → dim image
Projector shuts off after heating → cooling or ventilation
Image too large or small → sizing
Stretched or trapezoid image → distortion

sections.title: Objective 5.3 Exam Trap
paragraphs: Classify the symptom before selecting a fix. Several display problems can look similar while originating in different parts of the signal path.

entries.title: Input Source vs. Cable
paragraphs: Wrong input is a configuration problem. An image that changes when the cable moves is a physical-path problem.

entries.title: Fuzzy Image vs. Dead Pixel
paragraphs: Fuzzy affects image sharpness; a dead pixel is one fixed point.

entries.title: Dead Pixel vs. Burn-In
paragraphs: A dead pixel is an individual defect; burn-in is a retained image or pattern.

entries.title: Flashing vs. Burn-In
paragraphs: Flashing changes over time; burn-in remains static.

entries.title: Dim Image vs. Burnt-Out Bulb
paragraphs: A dim image remains visible. A burnt-out bulb cannot provide normal projector light, though a weakening bulb may become dim before failure.

entries.title: Projector Shutdown vs. Bulb
paragraphs: A projector that runs and later shuts down points toward heat or ventilation. A lamp that never illuminates points toward the bulb.
entries.memoryHook: RUNS THEN DIES → HEAT | NO LAMP → BULB

entries.title: Audio vs. Video
paragraphs: When video is correct but sound is missing, inspect audio output selection, volume, interface support, and speakers before replacing display hardware.

entries.title: Sizing vs. Distortion
paragraphs: Sizing changes overall dimensions; distortion changes shape or proportions.

entries.title: Fuzzy vs. Sizing
paragraphs: Both can involve resolution. Lack of sharpness means fuzzy; wrong physical display size means sizing.

sections.title: Display Troubleshooting Workflow
bullets: Classify the symptom: no signal, poor quality, panel defect, audio, projector, or geometry.
Trace the source, output, cable, input, and display in order.
Check resolution, scaling, aspect ratio, color, and audio settings.
Use the device-specific clue for monitor or projector problems.
Test known-good cables or displays when appropriate.
Apply the narrowest symptom term supported by the scenario.
sections.callout: SOURCE → CABLE → DISPLAY → SETTINGS → PROJECTOR → AUDIO
